card.description:
**Who We Are**

Capitol Aggregates, a division of Zachry, stands on a rich tradition of creativity, stability, innovation, and experience in the construction and building materials industry. Fully understanding that Capitols employees are the heart of our success, we foster a dynamic work environment by providing development opportunities such as training, education, and career advancement.

We believe people are our greatest asset and offer a variety of training and development opportunities to promote excellence and facilitate career advancement. We take care of our team members as family, within a culture of service where we do the right thing because it is the right thing to do.

**Our Core Values guide everything we do:**

Every Person Matters | Together We Can Do Great Things | This Is More Than a Job

**Position Overview**

The Plant Manager is responsible for overseeing the overall production, safety, maintenance, and employee management activities at the aggregate operations site. This role ensures operational excellence, regulatory compliance, and a strong culture of safety and environmental stewardship. The Plant Manager leads all aspects of site performance with a hands-on, collaborative approach, ensuring operational goals are met while building a high-performing team and delivering strong customer service.

**What Youll Do**

* Lead, plan, and direct daily plant operations including production, maintenance, and material handling.
* Manage production schedules, inventory controls, and key cost drivers to meet operational and financial targets.
* Lead employee life cycle activities including hiring, training, coaching, and performance management.
* Establish and enforce a strong safety culture ensuring compliance with MSHA, OSHA, environmental, and company standards.
* Monitor plant performance, operating costs, and efficiency to drive continuous improvement.
* Provide regular performance updates and strategic input to the Area Manager.

NOTE: This list presents only the principal duties of the position and is not intended to be comprehensive. Other duties and responsibilities may be assigned as dictated by the business needs and conditions. As an essential function of the job, good attendance is required.

**What Youll Bring**

**Required Skills and Abilities**

* Strong operational knowledge of aggregate production and equipment maintenance.
* Working knowledge of MSHA, OSHA, and environmental regulations.
* Proven ability to lead teams, set priorities, and deliver results.
* Strong problem-solving, organizational, and decision-making skills.
* Demonstrated commitment to safety leadership and operational excellence.

**Education & Experience**

* High School Diploma or GED required.
* Associate degree in Leadership, Supervision, Construction Management, Engineering, or a related field preferred.
* 1015 years of progressive experience in aggregates, mining, or heavy industrial operations required.
* 510 years of experience leading and managing teams in a plant or operations setting required.
* 35 years of direct maintenance experience within a plant environment required.
* Familiarity with the operation of mobile heavy equipment preferred.

**Other Qualifications**

* Consistent enforcement of safe work practices and PPE usage.
* Ability to interpret safety regulations, equipment manuals, and operational standards.
* Adaptability to changing operational demands and a collaborative, team-oriented approach.

**Leadership Expectations**

* Communicate the companys vision and values clearly to employees.
* Lead with integrity, professionalism, and sound judgment.
* Inspire a culture of safety, accountability, teamwork, and continuous improvement.
* Serve as a mentor and role model within the plant.

**Benefits & Equal Opportunity**

Capitol Aggregates offers an industry leading benefits package for our employees and their families.

* Medical, Dental, Vision and Life Insurance
* 401K, Paid Leave and Bonus Program
* Company-paid short-term and long-term disability insurance
* Employee assistance program
* Tuition Reimbursement
* And many more

We are an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, religion, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other legally protected status.

**Notice to Staffing Agencies**

Capitol Aggregates Inc. (Capitol) will not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. Any unsolicited resumes sent to Capitol, including unsolicited resumes sent to a Capitol mailing address or email address, directly to Capitol employees, or to Capitols resume database, will be considered Capitol property. Capitol will not pay a fee for any placement resulting from the receipt of an unsolicited resume. Capitol will consider any candidate for whom an Agency has submitted an unsolicited resume to have been referred by the Agency free of any charges or fees. Agencies must obtain advance written approval from Capitols recruiting function to submit resumes, and then only in conjunction with a valid, fully executed contract for service and in response to a specific job opening. Capitol will not pay a fee to any Agency that does not have such an agreement in place. Agency agreements will only be valid if in writing and signed by Capitols Human Resources Representative or their designee. No other Capitol employee is authorized to bind Capitol to any agreement regarding the placement of candidates by an Agency.

card.title: Senior Director, Engine & Plant Solutions Strategy
card.description:
**Job Description**
===================

This role defines how the GE Vernova Gas Power portfolio should evolve over a 5-year horizon and leads the front end of the hardware portfolio and NPI funnel. The leader converts shifts in customer needs, energy markets, technology, policy, competition, and adjacent value pools into an integrated portfolio architecture, prioritized opportunity pipeline, and decision-ready investment recommendations across heavy-duty gas turbines, aeroderivative gas turbines, steam turbines, generators, heat-recovery and balance-of-plant systems, equipment controls, and integrated engine and plant architectures.

 
 

The role matures outyear hardware and engine-solution opportunities until customer value, strategic fit, architecture, technical feasibility, economics, risk, ownership, and execution pathways are sufficiently defined for a Product Management decision. At that point, accountability transitions through a formal tollgate to Product Management, which owns funded commercialization, product roadmap execution, lifecycle performance, quality, delivery, and product cost.

 
 

Expected to work in a high intensity, sprint-based model, with high exposure to Power SLT on business-defining recommendations.

 
 

**Scope boundaries within the Strategy & Product Management team**
------------------------------------------------------------------

**Joint seams:** Data centers, distributed generation, hybrid systems and other cross-portfolio opportunities require a named lead by value proposition. This role leads when the core question is engine, equipment, controls or plant architecture; Software & Services Strategy leads when the core question is digital/services value capture; New Business Industrialization leads when the opportunity requires venture incubation or formation of a new business.

**Owned by New Business Industrialization:** Startup-like opportunities, external or emerging technologies requiring venture-style incubation, new business models, sandbox or stand-alone operating structures, early commercialization, and industrialization pathways outside the established hardware portfolio. This role may identify or sponsor a signal, but transfers venture incubation accountability.

**Owned by Software & Services Strategy:** Software products, industrial data and AI, digital platforms, recurring-revenue models, software-enabled services, services transformation, installed-base service strategy, and the enterprise value proposition that combines software, controls and services. This role supplies hardware and controls-interface requirements but does not own that strategy.

**Owned by this role:** Long-range hardware portfolio architecture; heavy-duty and aeroderivative engine platforms; steam, generator and balance-of-plant hardware; equipment controls and controls interfaces; new centerlines and derivatives; physical plant and power-island architectures; hardware competitiveness; and transition of defined opportunities into Product Management/NPI.

 
 

**Organizational scope**
------------------------

* Reports directly into the VP Power Strategy, with a formal operating interlock to the head of Product Management and the Power executive leadership team.

* Leads 4-6 direct reports plus cross-functional opportunity teams formed around priority initiatives.

* Global scope across new units, installed base, services, software and controls, digital offerings, engine and plant-system solutions, and selected adjacencies.

* Owns portfolio recommendations and incubation governance, not engineering line management, product P&Ls, commercial execution, or lifecycle delivery after transition.

* Decision rights include opportunity admission, evidence requirements, incubation funding recommendations, gate-readiness certification, and stop/pivot recommendations. Final investment approvals remain with designated business governance.

 
 

Required Qualifications

 
 

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering, business, economics, finance, computer science, or a related discipline.

* Typically 15+ years of progressively responsible experience across portfolio strategy, product management, engineering, technology commercialization, services, commercial strategy, or corporate/business strategy in complex industrial markets.

* Demonstrated leadership of enterprise-scale portfolio choices, new-platform evaluations, or integrated solution development involving material investment and multi-year uncertainty.

* Deep understanding of industrial product economics, lifecycle value, R&D/NPI governance, customer buying processes, and commercialization.

* Fluency in financial modeling, scenario analysis, business cases, capital allocation, and option-based decision making.

* Evidence of leading through influence across senior stakeholders with competing incentives and no direct reporting authority.

* Exceptional written and verbal executive communication, including the ability to simplify complex technical and market choices without losing rigor.

* Ability and willingness to engage customers globally and travel as required.

 
 

For candidates applying to a U.S. based position, the pay range for this position is between $248,000 and $341,000. The specific pay offered may be influenced by a variety of factors, including the candidate’s experience, education, and skill set.

Bonus eligibility: discretionary annual bonus

card.title: Director of Manufacturing Automation
card.description:
Karman Space & Defense is a leader in the rapid design, development, and production of critical, next-generation system solutions that align with the U.S. Department of War and its allies' core mission priorities, and meet the accelerating demand for access to space. Building on nearly 50 years of success, we deliver Payload & Protection Systems, Aero/Hydrodynamic Interstage Systems, and Propulsion & Launch Systems to more than 80 prime contractors supporting over 130 space and defense programs.

The Director of Manufacturing Automation leads the enterprise roadmap for practical, scalable automation across Karman manufacturing facilities. This leader partners with site operations, manufacturing engineering, quality, IT, and finance to identify high-return opportunities, pilot and deploy solutions, and sustain measurable improvements in safety, throughput, labor productivity, and quality. The role balances strategic technology selection with hands-on shop-floor execution and is accountable for standardizing successful solutions across multiple locations. 
 
**Responsibilities** 

* Develops and owns the enterprise manufacturing automation strategy, investment roadmap, and prioritized project portfolio.
* Identifies and quantifies automation opportunities through site assessments, capacity analysis, labor studies, and business cases with measurable returns.
* Leads implementation of robotics, CNC tending, automated inspection, material handling, and other fit-for-purpose production technologies.
* Partners with IT and cybersecurity teams on machine connectivity, industrial controls, data integrity, and secure integration with enterprise systems.
* Establishes standards for automation architecture, equipment acceptance, safety validation, commissioning, documentation, and maintainability.
* Coordinates cross-functional project teams and vendors to deliver automation installations within approved cost, schedule, and performance targets.
* Works with Quality and Engineering to validate automated processes, product conformity, and controlled changes in regulated manufacturing environments.
* Develops site technical capabilities through training, change management, and sustainable maintenance and support plans.
* Tracks automation performance using utilization, overall equipment effectiveness, cycle time, yield, labor hours, and realized financial benefits.
* Provides executive reporting on project status, risks, capital needs, and enterprise replication opportunities.

**Required Qualifications** 

* Bachelor's degree in engineering, manufacturing, automation, or a related technical discipline, or equivalent relevant experience.
* 10+ years of manufacturing engineering, industrial automation, or related technical experience, including 5+ years leading complex projects or teams.
* Demonstrated deployment of industrial automation solutions in discrete manufacturing environments.
* Experience developing capital business cases, managing vendors, and delivering projects against financial and operational targets.
* Working knowledge of industrial controls, robotics, machine interfaces, functional safety, and production data systems.
* Ability to lead across multiple sites and influence stakeholders without direct reporting authority.

**Preferred Qualifications** 

* Aerospace and defense manufacturing experience, including AS9100-controlled production.
* Experience with CNC automation, automated inspection, machine monitoring, and ERP/MES integration.
* Lean Six Sigma certification or demonstrated continuous improvement leadership.
* Advanced engineering degree or professional automation certification.

**Special Mentions** 

* Travel of up to 50% is required to Karman manufacturing facilities, suppliers, and project locations, based on business needs.
* Future relocation to a designated Karman location may be required based on evolving business needs. Any relocation expectations will be discussed with the employee in advance.
* Ability to work in active manufacturing environments and follow all site safety, security, and controlled-information procedures.

**Physical Requirements** 

* Regularly moves between office, production, and manufacturing engineering areas and uses computers and standard office equipment.
* Occasionally stands and walks for extended periods during shop-floor reviews and equipment assessments.
* The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

This role is part of our Space and Launch business, which has contributed to the nation's space programs for decades by delivering complete solutions from concept to flight. We enable successful space operations with mission-critical technology supporting every step from first launch to final landing, including launch vehicle subsystems, propulsion systems, aerodynamic and interstage systems, and payload protection and deployment. Our high-performance solutions are engineered to operate in the most extreme environments and meet precise mission requirements.

The Director of Production Planning leads the enterprise production planning and scheduling operating system across Karman's manufacturing operations. In this role, you will transform customer demand and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) outputs into executable production plans, capacity strategies, and recovery actions that support on-time delivery and predictable execution while providing visibility into risks, constraints, and opportunities across the manufacturing network.

**Responsibilities**

* Leads production planning, master scheduling, and finite-capacity planning across Karman manufacturing sites and value streams.
* Translates customer demand, backlog, and Sales, Inventory and Operations Planning (SIOP) outputs into achievable production schedules with clear priorities, constraints, and recovery plans.
* Establishes planning standards and key performance indicators (KPIs) for schedule adherence, on-time delivery, past-due backlog, work-in-process (WIP) aging, capacity utilization, and plan attainment.
* Partners with Operations and Manufacturing Engineering to align labor, equipment, tooling, and process capacity with production requirements.
* Coordinates with Supply Chain to identify material shortages, supplier constraints, and outside-processing risks before they affect production performance.
* Leads schedule recovery and re-baselining efforts when demand, material availability, quality issues, or capacity changes create delivery risk.
* Ensures enterprise resource planning (ERP), material requirements planning (MRP), and planning data are accurate, timely, and aligned with approved operating plans.
* Develops planners and schedulers while building a high-accountability planning organization.
* Provides executive visibility into delivery risk, capacity gaps, staffing needs, and critical decisions required to protect customer commitments.
* Improves end-to-end SIOP, planning, scheduling, and production-control processes.

**Required Qualifications**

* Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain, Operations, Engineering, Business, or a related field.
* 10+ years of production planning, master scheduling, operations planning, or supply chain experience in a manufacturing environment.
* 5+ years of leadership experience managing planning, scheduling, or production-control teams.
* Demonstrated experience with ERP, MRP, master production schedules, capacity planning, and material requirements planning.
* Strong analytical skills and experience leading cross-functional delivery-recovery plans.

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience in aerospace, defense, space, or other highly regulated manufacturing environments.
* Experience with SIOP, Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP), Power BI, or advanced manufacturing analytics.
* Knowledge of AS9100 and configuration-controlled manufacturing environments.

**Physical Requirements**

* Frequently communicates and works with employees in office and manufacturing environments.
* Frequently stands, walks, and uses a computer; occasionally bends, reaches, or moves throughout production areas as required by the role.
* The essential functions of this position must be performed with or without reasonable accommodation.

**Special Mentions**

* Frequent (25–50%) travel may be required to support Karman manufacturing sites.

This position requires U.S. person status under U.S. export control laws, including U.S. citizens and nationals, lawful permanent residents, refugees, and asylees.

* Medical, dental, and vision insurance
* 401(k) with company match
* Paid time off
* Health Savings Account (HSA) with company contribution
* Flexible Spending Accounts (FSA)
* Company‑paid life and AD&D insurance
* Short‑ and long‑term disability coverage
* Tuition reimbursement

card.title: Water Treatment Operations Supervisor Plant Manager
card.description:
**Join Inframark:** Leading the Way in Water Management
 
Inframark's Operations and Maintenance team is an award-winning team that delivers cutting-edge water, wastewater, and public works services to municipalities, utility districts, and industries. We are dedicated to supporting our employees as well as protecting the environment and the communities we serve. You would be empowered to thrive in a dynamic, supportive, and innovative environment. Take the next step in your career and join us at Inframark. Apply today!
 
Why Work for Inframark?
 
 
Our dedication to sustainability and community impact drives us to ensure clean, safe water for future generations. Whether you're at the start of your career or looking for advancement, Inframark offers purpose-driven work and opportunities for growth. We offer an attractive salary package, including a generous benefits package with health, dental, and life insurance, 401(k) plan, paid time off, sick leave, holidays, and wellness plan.
 
 
Water Operations Supervisor
 
Jasper GA
 
Are you an experienced water professional ready to take the next step in leadership? We are seeking a Water Operations Supervisor to oversee the day-to-day operation, maintenance, and regulatory compliance of our water treatment and distribution systems. In this role, you'll lead a skilled team, ensure safe and efficient plant operations, and play a critical role in delivering high-quality drinking water to the communities we serve.
 
This is an excellent opportunity for a licensed water treatment professional who thrives in a hands-on leadership role and is passionate about operational excellence, team development, and public service.
 
What You'll Do
 
 
**As the Water Operations Supervisor, you will:** 

* Lead the continuous operation of water treatment plants, wells, standpipes, distribution systems, and related infrastructure.
* Supervise and support operations staff, ensuring work is completed safely, efficiently, and in compliance with all regulatory requirements.
* Monitor plant performance and operational processes, making adjustments as needed to maintain system reliability and water quality.
* Prepare and review internal, regulatory, and client reports.
* Verify staff compliance with operational procedures, maintenance programs, laboratory protocols, QA/QC standards, and safety requirements.
* Conduct regular meetings with department leaders to review performance metrics, operational goals, and continuous improvement opportunities.
* Assist in establishing facility objectives, operational strategies, and workforce planning initiatives.
* Respond effectively to emergency situations and implement corrective actions when necessary.
* Champion a strong safety culture by overseeing and enforcing company safety programs and standards.
* Participate in hiring, interviewing, onboarding, coaching, performance evaluations, and disciplinary processes.
* Develop and approve staff schedules to ensure adequate operational coverage.
* Support budgeting, planning, and administrative functions.
* Serve as acting Project Manager when needed.
* Build positive relationships with customers, clients, municipal officials, and community stakeholders.

What We're Looking For
 
Required Qualifications
 

* High school diploma or GED required.
* Additional college coursework or vocational training in chemistry, environmental science, water technology, or a related field preferred.
* Minimum of five (5) years of experience in water treatment, water distribution, system maintenance, construction, or related utility operations.
* Class I Water Treatment Plant Operator License (or equivalent license required by the state of employment).
* Valid driver's license with an acceptable driving record.

Knowledge & Experience
 
 
**Successful candidates will have knowledge of:** 

* Surface water treatment processes and groundwater operations.
* Water quality regulations, permits, and compliance requirements.
* Pumps, motors, valves, engines, and related mechanical equipment.
* Backflow prevention devices and cross-connection control practices.
* Supervising, mentoring, and developing employees.
* Utility operations, maintenance planning, and emergency response procedures.

Skills for Success
 

* Strong leadership and team development capabilities.
* Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
* Ability to evaluate operating parameters and optimize treatment processes.
* Experience operating process control systems and laboratory equipment.
* Strong analytical, troubleshooting, and decision-making abilities.

Work Environment
 
This role combines office responsibilities with field and plant operations. You will work in both indoor and outdoor environments and may be exposed to changing weather conditions, mechanical equipment, chemicals, noise, dust, and other industrial settings. Appropriate safety procedures and personal protective equipment are required.
 
Physical Requirements
 

* Ability to stand, walk, climb, bend, kneel, crouch, and work around operational equipment for extended periods.
* Frequently lift, carry, push, or pull up to 50 pounds.
* Ability to work in confined spaces and elevated areas when required.
* Must be able to distinguish between different shades of color for operational and safety purposes.
* Available to work overtime and respond to emergency situations outside normal business hours, including weekends and holidays when necessary

To support a safe and secure workplace, all offers of employment are contingent upon the successful completion of background screening, drug testing, and driving record review where applicable.
 
Inframark is an Equal Opportunity Employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, color, age, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, or protected veteran status and will not be discriminated against based on disability.

card.title: Director of the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences Institute
card.description:
**Department**
--------------

College of Aerospace, Computing, Engineering, and Design

**About the University**

 

Established in 1965, Metropolitan State University ( MSU Denver ) was founded to serve students who were underrepresented in higher education whose life paths and experiences did not fit the traditional mold. Sixty years later, the University continues to serve over 16,000 of Colorado’s extraordinary and diverse students, providing them with the foundation on which to build their unique aspirations. As the third largest public institution of higher education in Colorado, MSU Denver is a model university for today’s college students.

Proud of its federal designation as a Hispanic-Serving Institution that also offers graduate programs (gHSI) and the only Seal of Excelencia certified institution in Colorado, the University serves the most diverse undergraduate student population in the state, as well as the most first-generation students. Through affordable, flexible, and holistic education, MSU Denver helps students build essential skills grounded in a multicultural and global perspective that lead to undergraduate and graduate degrees, and career and life success.

 

At MSU Denver, we are committed to our CADRE values: Community, Access, Diversity, Respect, and Excellence. We strive to create a supportive and inclusive environment where all community members are valued and belong. Our dedication to breaking down barriers to education, fostering open dialogue, and promoting world-class scholarship ensures that we provide exceptional services and innovative learning opportunities for our students, faculty, and staff.

 

**Position Summary**

 

MSU Denver seeks a Director to lead the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences Institute ( AMSI ) and advance its development into a sustainable, impactful program. The Director manages all AMSI activities including the Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence which serves Colorado manufacturers through technology demonstrations, training, micro-credentials, and sponsored partnerships. The Director is the primary liaison and point of contact for all industry partners. The Director develops and maintains the Advanced Manufacturing Sciences academic programs in collaboration with various academic departments.

The Director builds integrated pathways for both degree-seeking students and non-degree learners. These pathways connect credentials, work-based learning, undergraduate and graduate programs, and lifelong learning. The Director also makes AMSI a hub for interdisciplinary collaboration within CACED and across the University. Through AMSI, the Director connects academic programs, faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations around shared learning, applied research, workforce development, and emerging opportunities.

A high priority for the Director is to develop a long-term model that allows AMSI to sustain and grow its programs and activities beyond short-term or one-time funding. The incoming Director will build appropriate revenue-generating activities to support students, programs, equipment, and future growth.

 

**Responsibilities**

 

Institute Strategy

* Set and carry out AMSI’s mission, vision, and annual plan consistent with the strategy, budgets, goals, and policies of CACED and the University.
* Advance industry-relevant technologies, practices, and partnerships that prepare students to contribute from their first day on the job and that address manufacturing workforce gaps.
Maintain an active Advisory Board and keep it informed through an outcomes dashboard that tracks sponsors, student credit hours, enrollments, non-degree learners served, placements, revenue by source, and other appropriate data. 

Institute Sustainability

* Develop a long-term sustainability model and a multi-year business plan that sets out AMSI’s costs, funding sources, and revenue sources; update the plan each year.
* Build a diversified funding base that combines earned revenue, industry partnerships and sponsorships, philanthropy, and public and private grants.
* Develop appropriate revenue-generating activities that are consistent with the University’s mission and strategic plan.
* Oversee fee-based manufacturing services offered by AMSI.
* Pursue grants and other funding that build lasting capacity and plan how successful grant-funded programs and positions will continue after the award ends.
Partner with the Office of Sponsored Research and Projects and Advancement on identifying and applying for grants, gifts, corporate sponsorships, equipment and donations. 

Integrated Learning Pathways

* Work with faculty and academic departments to identify where micro-credentials, industry-recognized credentials, and competency-based training can be included in academic certificates and degrees consistent with University curriculum and credit policies.
* Expand work-based learning with manufacturing employers including internships, apprenticeships, industry-sponsored capstones, and applied projects.
* Strengthen the path from AMS undergraduate programs into graduate study and 4+1 programs.
* Create upskilling and reskilling training opportunities for incumbent workers and adult learners that offer clear entry points into credit-bearing programs.
Establish transfer and articulation agreements with community colleges and other educational partners. 

Interdisciplinary Collaboration

* Bring faculty and students from CACED’s aerospace, computing, engineering, and design programs, and from other appropriate academic programs, together with industry partners on sponsored projects, capstones, applied research, and grant proposals.
* Open AMSI’s labs, equipment, and industry relationships to academic programs across the University for teaching and applied research opportunities.
Host and participate in convenings and working groups that bring faculty, students, industry partners, and community organizations together on workforce development and emerging technologies. 

Industry 4.0 Center of Excellence

* Lead and grow the COE’s fee-for-service and manufacturing services programs through technology demonstrations, corporate training (standard and custom), micro-credentials and certificates, applied research and development, capstone sponsorships, and selective lab and equipment access.
* Draw on manufacturing networks including CAMA, WiM, Manufacturer’s Edge, and MWAMA, and on state and federal funding opportunities, to convene industry partners, launch programs, and generate applied industry projects.
Standardize scoping, intellectual property, safety, and performance-metric templates for company projects. 

Academic Programs

* Develop and maintain the AMS academic programs with faculty and department leaders and keep curricula current with industry needs through regular input from industry partners.
* Oversee student recruitment, retention, and job placement goals and activities.
Coordinate internship placements, serve as internship advisor, and manage internship evaluations and reporting. 

Laboratory Operations

* Oversee AMSI labs and testbeds for safe, scheduled use by multiple academic programs and expand their use for industry collaboration and applied research.
Plan equipment maintenance, upgrades, and replacement so that AMSI’s technology stays current with industry practice. 

Administration

* Supervise, evaluate, and develop AMSI staff and direct their work on the Institute’s priorities in lab operations, business operations, workforce development initiatives, student recruitment and retention, and marketing and communications.
* Prepare annual reports, budget plans, and periodic reviews and maintain sound financial management and risk controls.
Manage memoranda of understanding and other agreements with academic units and external partners. 

 

**Position Competencies**

* Champions CADRE values-based leadership and creates a positive workplace culture, by setting expectations, eliciting feedback and coaching across departments, ensuring accountability and excelling in conflict management
* Aligns operations across teams by optimizing resources, maintaining compliance, and empowering leaders to deliver consistent, measurable outcomes
* Translates University strategy into coordinated action by guiding decision-making, prioritizing initiatives, and adjusting plans to drive long-term progress
* Builds cross-functional partnerships, sharing information widely and facilitating dialogue to break down silos and advance University goals
* Creates a positive workplace culture of belonging by embedding equitable leadership and talent processes, fostering feedback and holding leaders accountable
Drives innovation by aligning initiatives to University priorities, anticipating change, and empowering leaders to implement sustainable improvements 

 

**Required Qualifications**

* Master’s degree from an accredited institution or an equivalent combination of education and experience
* Working knowledge of advanced manufacturing technologies and the workforce needs of manufacturing employers
* Familiarity with Colorado’s manufacturing employers, industry associations, and workforce funding programs
Experience supervising staff and managing budgets that draw on multiple funding sources, such as grants, contracts, gifts, or earned revenue 

**Preferred Qualifications**

* Experience building credential programs, apprenticeships, or other work-based learning that connects to degree programs
* A record of leading interdisciplinary initiatives with faculty and partners from multiple disciplines or organizations
* Experience securing state, federal, or foundation grants, and sustaining programs after grant funding ends
* Industry experience in manufacturing, aerospace, or a related sector
Experience in higher education with diverse, urban student populations 

 

We encourage you to apply even if you do not meet every preferred qualification. We are most interested in finding the candidate who will best contribute to the AMSI Institute, our mission, and the University.

**Schedule Information**

* Full time, 40 hrs/wk
* Exempt
* Days of the Week: Monday - Friday, during regular University business hours that typically range between 8:00 am - 5:00 pm
* Evenings and Weekend Work: As needed for industry events, University events, meetings, and other program activities
* Schedule: Primarily in person on campus with some flexibility for remote work depending upon program needs and supervisor approval
Travel: Local travel as needed for industry partnerships, employer engagement, and related activities, with occasional travel for conferences or professional development 

 

**Salary for Announcement**

 

Under Colorado law, MSU Denver is required to provide a reasonable estimate of the compensation range for this role and should not offer a salary outside of the range posted in this job announcement. With over 30 yrs. in the Landscape Rock and Construction Materials Supplier industry, **MDI ROCK** continues to be the largest family owned Landscape Supply Company in Arizona. With locations in Phoenix, Prescott, Queen Creek, Dewey, and Ash Fork.

**MDI ROCK** is currently seeking a **PLANT MANAGER** for our Dewey Rock Quarry located in **DEWEY, AZ**.

The Plant Manager will oversee all daily operations of the plant from production and manufacturing to ensuring employees meet company standards for Safety, Quality, and efficiency.

**Responsibilities**

* Plan, organize, direct and run optimum day-to-day operations to exceed our customers’ expectations
* Increase production, assets capacity and flexibility while minimizing unnecessary costs and maintaining current quality standards
* Be responsible for production output, product quality and on-time shipping
* Allocate resources effectively and fully utilize assets to produce optimal results
* Implement strategies in alignment with strategic initiatives and provide a clear sense of direction and focus
* Monitor operations and trigger corrective actions
* Share a trusting relationship with workgroup and recruit, manage and develop plant staff
* Develop systems and processes that track and optimize productivity and standards, metrics and performance targets to ensure effective return on assets
* Operate loaders, rock trucks, excavators, and drilling equipment

* Proven work experience as a plant manager
* Working knowledge and understanding of MSHA regulations and possess a strong personal commitment to safety believing all incidents are preventable
* Understanding of aggregate processing and equipment
* Excellent verbal, written and interpersonal communication skills and capable of developing and maintaining good relationships with company and regulatory agency personnel
* Knowledge of ATF and ADEQ laws and requirements
* Ability to create accountability and to lead by example
* Strong team building, decision-making and people management skills

* Medical, Dental, and Vision after 90 days

card.title: Digital Plant Manager
card.description:
Some people manage teams. Others build environments where elite technical talent thrives, innovation accelerates, and customers become lifelong advocates. We’re looking for a Digital Plant Manager who can do all three.

This isn’t a “keep the trains running” management role. We need a leader who can build and steward high-performing Agile teams, drive operational excellence, own financial outcomes, and help shape the future of Vertech’s Digital Plant organization. You’ll lead self-organizing Scrum teams delivering world class industrial automation and software solutions while guiding strategic investments in internal development tools and accelerators that improve how we work and scale.

If you know how to balance leadership with accountability, coaching with execution, and strategy with action—and you genuinely enjoy helping talented people do the best work of their careers—we should probably talk.

**Who We Are**

At Vertech, not only do we develop world class industrial automation solutions for some of the top US companies, we also strive to be the team of choice for the best and brightest talent. I mean, we call ourselves control freaks for a reason.

The passion (and intelligence) our employees have is truly mind-blowing. In turn, we work hard to take care of our own with excellent benefits and pay, personal development, and transparent communication. We also know that you can be great at what you do and still have fun.

If that sounds like a good fit, help us bring the next generation of automation solutions to industries including data centers, renewable energy, manufacturing, food and beverage, water and wastewater, and more.

**Top Reasons to Work with Us**

* Flexible work schedule with work from home options for many roles
* Weekly communication from management in our internally famous Friday morning meeting
* Competitive compensation including a bonus plan
* No more than a 4 week waiting period on all benefits including the 401k
* A really rad Christmas Party each year
* A manager that is cool…most of the time, because no one is perfect
* A path for growth, a great culture, PTO, AND MORE!

**What You Will Be Doing**

* Build, lead, and develop high-performing Professional Scrum teams capable of delivering world class customer outcomes
* Coach, mentor, and support team members through consistent feedback, career development, and leadership
* Ensure teams are staffed with the right people in the right roles while fostering Vertech’s culture and core values
* Own the financial performance and delivery outcomes of projects executed by your teams
* Serve as the primary escalation point for customers beyond the execution team
* Drive operational excellence using Professional Agile Leadership (PAL-E), Scrum principles, and Evidence Based Management (EBM)
* Govern and prioritize Digital Plant’s portfolio of internal software accelerators and development tools
* Partner with leadership to contribute to strategic planning and organizational growth initiatives
* Ensure investment initiatives are properly staffed, organized, funded, and aligned with company objectives
* Promote continuous improvement in delivery execution, technical excellence, and team collaboration
* Work closely with HR and leadership on hiring, onboarding, employee growth, and team performance
* Help create an environment where highly technical people genuinely enjoy coming to work

**What You Need for this Position**

* Bachelor’s degree in engineering or related technical field (or equivalent industry experience)
* Deep expertise in Agile frameworks, Professional Scrum, and Professional Agile Leadership (PAL-E)
* 7+ years of experience in industrial automation and systems integration
* 3+ years of leadership experience with accountability for team success
* Strong understanding of software and industrial systems development methodologies including Agile, DevOps, CI/CD, and related practices
* Proven ability to lead technical teams while balancing customer satisfaction, delivery quality, and financial performance
* Excellent communication, organizational, and leadership skills
* Strong business acumen including understanding of project financials, margins, utilization, and operational efficiency

**Bonus Points If You Have**

* Experience leading multiple Scrum teams simultaneously
* Background in software product or platform development
* Experience scaling Agile delivery organizations
* Passion for coaching and developing technical talent
* A desire to build systems and teams that continuously improve over time

**Why This Role Matters**

The Digital Plant Manager plays a critical role in Vertech’s vision to be recognized as a world class provider of industrial automation services—and the employer of choice for top talent. This role directly influences our people, our customers, our delivery capabilities, and the future of how we scale Digital Plant operations.

No pressure. But also…kind of a big deal.

card.title: Director of Quality and Accreditation
card.description:
Overview:

We are seeking a dynamic and experienced Director of Quality and Accreditation to lead our facility’s efforts in ensuring the highest standards of patient care and safety. This leadership role is responsible for overseeing regulatory compliance, quality assurance programs, and continuous improvement initiatives across all clinical and operational areas. The Director will guide the development and implementation of quality protocols, manage accreditation processes, and lead the Quality Assurance and Process Improvement (QAPI) program. The ideal candidate will be a proactive, strategic thinker with a strong commitment to achieving excellence in care delivery and regulatory readiness.

**PURPOSE STATEMENT:**

The Director of Quality and Accreditation is responsible for ensuring patient safety and superior quality of care as measured by survey readiness, treatment program fidelity, and compliance with state and federal laws and regulations and accreditation standards. As such, the Director is responsible for leading and overseeing all aspects of policy development; comprehensive implementation of Acadia’s prescribed clinical protocols, operational quality oversight standards, and programmatic expectations; critical incident reporting; regulatory engagement, including development and submission of plans of correction; certification achievement and maintenance; oversight of the quality assurance and process improvement (QAPI) program; and on-going regulatory readiness strategies at the facility. Through routine physical presence in patient care areas, data analysis and documentation monitoring, and intentional sharing of deep subject-matter expertise, the Director will ensure a proactive, multidisciplinary focus on quality and excellence within the facility.

Responsibilities:

**ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS:**

* Lead and monitor day-to-day regulatory readiness, patient safety, and service excellence across the facility.
* QAPI program oversight and management – follow and develop processes for identification, collection, and analysis of quality performance data.
 + Utilize collected data regarding the outcome of activities for delivering continuously improving services.
 + Conduct annual preparation and evaluation of the facility QAPI Program.
 + Complete process improvement projects and incorporate the results into patient care improvements.
 + Submit quality scorecard data to Acadia corporate office as requested.
 + Coordinate the abstraction of clinical data according to Joint Commission specifications and data entry via vendor database for Inpatient Psychiatric Core Measures (ex. national quality measures such as HBIPS).
 + Identify key aspects of care relevant indicators and evaluation of data using formal and informal feedback from consumers of services and other collateral sources is aggregated and used to improve management strategies and service delivery practices.
 + Lead/coordinate data collection and analysis from all departments within the facility.
 + Prepare and present program data trends and action plans to the monthly Quality Council and quarterly to the Medical Executive Committee and the Governing Board.

card.title: Quality Systems Project Sr Manager
card.description:
At Zimmer Biomet, we believe in pushing the boundaries of innovation and driving our mission forward. As a global medical technology leader for nearly 100 years, a patient’s mobility is enhanced by a Zimmer Biomet product or technology every 8 seconds.

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talented team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels inspired, invested, cared for, valued, and have a strong sense of belonging.

**What You Can Expect**
-----------------------

Leads the Quality Management System (QMS) integration of acquired medical device businesses and/or products into Zimmer Biomet (ZB) network. Plans, manages and executes the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) to update, harmonize and transition the acquired site’s QMS to ZB Global Quality requirements and applicable regulations; to remediate and transfer the site’s QMS and medical device product quality documentation and records from legacy systems into ZB global enterprise IT applications; and to ensure the site obtains and/or maintains certifications and establishment registration. Partners cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Operations, Supplier Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, Servicing, IT, the Integration Management Office (IMO) and acquired-site leadership to complete integration on schedule and within budget while maintaining continuous regulatory compliance, product supply and in-process regulatory submissions.

**How You'll Create Impact**
----------------------------

* Leads cross-functional, multi-workstream QMS integration projects for newly acquired medical device businesses, from post-close planning through harmonization, documentation transfer, verification of effectiveness and integration closure.
 + Serves as the ZB Quality Integration Lead / QMS Project Leader for assigned acquisitions; accountable for the integration plan, schedule, budget, resources and deliverables.
 + Proposes corporate-wide process and issue solutions; resolves conflicts and escalates risks and roadblocks to Quality leadership and the IMO.
 + Coaches and mentors ZB and acquired-site team members on ZB Global QMS requirements; may supervise or direct team members, contractors and consultants.
 + Reviewer and approver of integration plans, gap assessments, migration protocols/reports and document-controlled forms.
 + Serves as Global SME for the QMS integration process and as site SME for multiple QMS sub-systems during transition.
 + Represents Quality in external and internal (global, site, IMO and executive) meetings, and during regulatory inspections and certification audits related to integration.
 + Strategic project planning for projects of all scale and complexity (plan, resources, budget).
* QMS Integration Planning and Project Management:
 + Translates due diligence findings into integration scope, risk-based priorities and workstreams; authors and maintains the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) per ZB global integration guidance and M&A procedures, and obtains cross-functional approval of the plan and its revisions.
 + Establishes and leads integration workstreams (e.g., Management Controls; Document & Record Controls & QMS Software; Design & Development Controls & Risk Management; Servicing; Purchasing, Production & Process Controls; CAPA / Quality Systems; Post-Market Surveillance; Regulatory and Clinical Affairs), assigning ZB and site owners, milestones and target dates.
 + Maintains detailed integration action plans, schedules and risk/issue logs (e.g., SharePoint, Smartsheet); leads recurring integration project meetings and reports status, budget, timeline, risks and roadblocks to Quality leadership, the IMO and site senior leadership.
 + Manages the integration budget and resource plan (including incremental headcount and external support) and revises the IPP when scope changes (e.g., new markets, new NPI projects, new product registrations).
* QMS Harmonization and Transition:
 + Leads gap assessments of site QMS procedures, processes and records against the ZB Global Quality Manual, global procedures (GBL/GBLW), and applicable regulations and standards; documents the harmonization approach and remediation actions.
 + Drives revision, adoption or retirement of the site Quality Manual, Quality Policy, procedures and work instructions; defines interim controls, “hybridized” processes, workstream decision forms and design control transition memoranda to maintain compliance until full adoption of global requirements.
 + Coordinates implementation of management controls, including Management Representative designation, organization charts and job descriptions, global KPIs and Global Quality Report, management review, and internal/external audit programs.
 + Establishes stakeholder-agreed cutover / go-live dates for each QMS sub-system (e.g., document control, CAPA, nonconformance, product holds, HHE/field actions, complaints, supplier controls, calibration, servicing) and ensures open legacy records are completed and closed under legacy procedures.
 + Coordinates intercompany quality agreements between the acquired site and ZB sites (e.g., complaint handling units, distribution and service centers) and contract manufacturers.

**How You'll Create Impact (cont.)**
------------------------------------

* Documentation Remediation and Transfer to ZB Enterprise Applications:
 + Plans and leads the transfer of QMS and product quality documentation and records from the acquired site’s legacy eQMS/document management system into ZB global enterprise applications (e.g., Windchill, OpenText LiveLink, WOW, Codebeamer, EtQ Reliance, iLearn, ServiceMax).
 + Develops data migration / transfer protocols, data mapping, acceptance criteria, verification and summary reports; ensures migrated and archived records remain complete, accurate, retrievable and compliant with record retention and electronic records/signature requirements.
 + Assesses and remediates product quality documentation, including Design History Files (DHF), Risk Management Files (RMF), Device Master Records, labeling, specifications and drawings, validations (process, software, test method) and supplier files (e.g., ASL, SPPA, SCN, SCAR), to ZB global requirements before or during transfer.
 + Coordinates with R&D and Regulatory Affairs to sequence documentation transfer so that ongoing NPI, design transfer and regulatory submissions (e.g., 510(k)) are not disrupted.
 + Partners with IT and global system owners on site set-up (e.g., site codes, user access, configuration), system training for site personnel, training curricula mapping to the ZB learning management system, and legacy system archival and decommissioning.
* Compliance, Effectiveness and Closure:
 + Ensures continued compliance and inspection readiness throughout the transition; initiates IE, CAPA or equivalent when gaps represent substantial noncompliance to regulatory requirements.
 + Supports site certification readiness (e.g., ISO 13485, MDSAP) and preparation for the post-integration corporate QMS audit.
 + Plans verification of effectiveness of integration activities (e.g., internal or independent QMS audit), drives closure of resulting nonconformances, and authors the IPP closure summary.
 + Captures lessons learned and continuously improves the ZB global QMS integration process, templates and playbook.

*This is not an exhaustive list of duties or functions and might not necessarily comprise all of the essential functions for purposes of the Americans with Disabilities Act.*

**What Makes You Stand Out**
----------------------------

* Expert knowledge of medical device QMS requirements: FDA 21 CFR Part 820, 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR, MDSAP and other global regulations.
* Broad working knowledge of all QMS sub-systems: document and record control, design controls, risk management, CAPA, nonconformance, complaints/MDR, HHE/field actions, supplier controls, process and software validation, calibration, servicing and post-market surveillance.
* Proven program/project management of complex, multi-workstream, cross-functional projects (scope, schedule, budget, resources, risk and change control).
* Experience with M&A integration, site transfers/consolidations, or QMS harmonization and remediation.
* Hands-on experience with enterprise eQMS/PLM applications (e.g., Windchill, EtQ, OpenText, Codebeamer, Greenlight Guru), data migration and computer system validation.
* Strong knowledge of DHF, RMF, DMR and technical documentation content and structure.
* Ability to lead and influence without direct authority and to manage organizational change and cultural transition at acquired sites.
* Excellent executive-level communication, facilitation and status reporting.
* Sound risk-based judgement, problem solving and decision making in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.
* Excellent technical writing skills.
* Proficient with project management and reporting tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, SharePoint, Tableau/Power BI).

**Your Background**
-------------------

* Bachelor's Degree and 5 years of relevant experience, or Associate's Degree and 7 years of relevant experience, or High School Diploma or Equivalent and 9 years of relevant experience required.
* B.S. in Engineering, Life Sciences or related field preferred.
* Advanced degree (M.S./MBA) preferred.
* 10+ years in medical device Quality / Quality Systems or equivalent experience, including 5+ years leading cross-functional projects highly preferred.
* Experience leading QMS integration, harmonization or remediation for acquisitions, site transfers or eQMS/PLM implementations strongly preferred.
* PMP or equivalent project management certification preferred.
* ASQ CQA, CQE or CMQ/OE, or ISO 13485 / MDSAP Lead Auditor certification preferred.
* Lean / Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred.
* Experience with SiMD/SaMD, robotics or capital equipment preferred.

**Travel Expectations**
-----------------------

* Up to 30% (domestic and international travel to acquired sites and ZB locations)

**Expected Compensation Range**
-------------------------------

$128,000 - $160,000 USD Annually

As a Zimmer Biomet team member, you will share in our commitment to providing mobility and renewed life to people around the world. To support our talented team, we focus on development opportunities, robust employee resource groups (ERGs), a flexible working environment, location specific competitive total rewards, wellness incentives and a culture of recognition and performance awards. We are committed to creating an environment where every team member feels inspired, invested, cared for, valued, and have a strong sense of belonging.

**What You Can Expect**
-----------------------

Leads the Quality Management System (QMS) integration of acquired medical device businesses and/or products into Zimmer Biomet (ZB) network. Plans, manages and executes the QMS Integration Project Plan (IPP) to update, harmonize and transition the acquired site’s QMS to ZB Global Quality requirements and applicable regulations; to remediate and transfer the site’s QMS and medical device product quality documentation and records from legacy systems into ZB global enterprise IT applications; and to ensure the site obtains and/or maintains certifications and establishment registration. Partners cross-functionally with Quality, Regulatory, R&D, Operations, Supplier Quality, Post-Market Surveillance, Servicing, IT, the Integration Management Office (IMO) and acquired-site leadership to complete integration on schedule and within budget while maintaining continuous regulatory compliance, product supply and in-process regulatory submissions.

**How You'll Create Impact**
----------------------------

* Leads cross-functional, multi-workstream QMS integration projects for newly acquired medical device businesses, from post-close planning through harmonization, documentation transfer, verification of effectiveness and integration closure.

 + Coaches and mentors ZB and acquired-site team members on ZB Global QMS requirements; may supervise or direct team members, contractors and consultants.
 + Reviewer and approver of integration plans, gap assessments, migration protocols/reports and document-controlled forms.

 + Plans verification of effectiveness of integration activities (e.g., internal or independent QMS audit), drives closure of resulting nonconformances, and authors the IPP closure summary.
 + Captures lessons learned and continuously improves the ZB global QMS integration process, templates and playbook.

----------------------------

* Expert knowledge of medical device QMS requirements: FDA 21 CFR Part 820, 21 CFR Part 11, ISO 13485, ISO 14971, EU MDR, MDSAP and other global regulations.
* Broad working knowledge of all QMS sub-systems: document and record control, design controls, risk management, CAPA, nonconformance, complaints/MDR, HHE/field actions, supplier controls, process and software validation, calibration, servicing and post-market surveillance.
* Proven program/project management of complex, multi-workstream, cross-functional projects (scope, schedule, budget, resources, risk and change control).
* Experience with M&A integration, site transfers/consolidations, or QMS harmonization and remediation.
* Hands-on experience with enterprise eQMS/PLM applications (e.g., Windchill, EtQ, OpenText, Codebeamer, Greenlight Guru), data migration and computer system validation.
* Strong knowledge of DHF, RMF, DMR and technical documentation content and structure.
* Ability to lead and influence without direct authority and to manage organizational change and cultural transition at acquired sites.
* Excellent executive-level communication, facilitation and status reporting.
* Sound risk-based judgement, problem solving and decision making in ambiguous, fast-changing environments.
* Excellent technical writing skills.
* Proficient with project management and reporting tools (e.g., MS Project, Smartsheet, SharePoint, Tableau/Power BI).

**Your Background**
-------------------

* Bachelor's Degree and 5 years of relevant experience, or Associate's Degree and 7 years of relevant experience, or High School Diploma or Equivalent and 9 years of relevant experience required.
* B.S. in Engineering, Life Sciences or related field preferred.
* Advanced degree (M.S./MBA) preferred.
* 10+ years in medical device Quality / Quality Systems or equivalent experience, including 5+ years leading cross-functional projects highly preferred.
* Experience leading QMS integration, harmonization or remediation for acquisitions, site transfers or eQMS/PLM implementations strongly preferred.
* PMP or equivalent project management certification preferred.
* ASQ CQA, CQE or CMQ/OE, or ISO 13485 / MDSAP Lead Auditor certification preferred.
* Lean / Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt preferred.
* Experience with SiMD/SaMD, robotics or capital equipment preferred.

-----------------------

* Up to 30% (domestic and international travel to acquired sites and ZB locations)

-------------------------------

$128,000 - $160,000 USD Annually

card.title: Director Food Safety and Quality
card.description:
Job Summary
 
The Director, Food Safety & Quality is a senior, project-based individual contributor who is deployed to the most critical food safety and quality priorities across Maker’s Pride’s manufacturing network. Rather than leading a team, this leader goes where the need is greatest: stepping into facilities, programs, and issues that require immediate expertise, rapidly assessing the situation, and leading cross-functional teams to resolution without direct authority. Working in close partnership with plant leadership, Operations, Engineering, Supply Chain, Product Development, Sanitation, and plant FSQA teams, the Director stabilizes high-risk areas, solves complex problems, and builds sustainable capability so improvements hold after the engagement ends. This role serves as a senior technical decision-maker on food safety risk and represents the company with regulators, key customers, and certification bodies on escalated matters.
 
 
Key Responsibilities
 
Critical Site & Program Interventions
 

* Deploy to facilities, lines, and programs identified as highest risk or underperforming, often on short notice, to assess conditions and lead immediate stabilization.
* Rapidly diagnose root causes of food safety and quality gaps and develop clear, prioritized action plans with plant leadership.
* Lead cross-functional plant teams through execution of improvement plans, removing barriers and escalating risks as needed.
* Transition sustainable processes, tools, and ownership to site leadership before exiting each engagement.

Project Leadership & Prioritization
 

* Lead a portfolio of high-impact food safety and quality projects, defining scope, objectives, milestones, and success measures for each.
* Partner with the VP of HSE, FSQA to prioritize engagements based on enterprise risk, business impact, and customer or regulatory exposure.
* Manage multiple concurrent projects across sites, adjusting priorities quickly as new critical issues emerge.
* Provide regular project status, risk updates, and outcomes to the VP of HSE, FSQA and executive leadership.

Food Safety Risk Management & Decision-Making
 

* Serve as a senior technical decision-maker on food safety risk, including product hold, release, and disposition decisions.
* Lead or support the company’s response to food safety incidents, including recall and market withdrawal events, in partnership with senior leadership.
* Lead risk assessments and management of change reviews for high-risk changes to ingredients, processes, equipment, packaging, and facilities.
* Ensure HACCP, HARPC, and Preventive Controls programs at engaged sites are effectively designed, validated, and maintained.

**Technical Expertise:** Allergen Control, Sanitary Design & Complaints
 

* Address high-risk allergen control gaps, including labeling controls, scheduling, segregation, and cleaning validation and verification.
* Provide sanitary design expertise on critical equipment, facility, and capital projects, and ensure food safety requirements are incorporated.
* Lead investigations into significant or recurring customer and consumer complaints, driving root cause analysis and effective CAPA to closure.

External Relationships & Audit Readiness
 

* Represent Maker’s Pride with regulatory agencies, key customers, and certification bodies on escalated food safety matters.
* Lead sites through high-stakes regulatory inspections, customer audits, and GFSI-benchmarked certification audits (e.g., SQF, BRCGS), including remediation of findings.
* Support commercial teams in resolving critical customer quality concerns.

Sustainability & Network Learning
 

* Define success measures for each engagement and verify that improvements are sustained after transition.
* Capture lessons learned and translate solutions into standards, tools, and best practices that can be applied across the network.
* Identify systemic risks across engagements and recommend enterprise-level actions to prevent recurrence.

**Qualifications:** 
**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in Food Science, Engineering, Microbiology, Chemistry, Biological Sciences, or related discipline required.
 
 
**Experience:** 

* 10+ years of experience in food manufacturing, quality, engineering, or food safety required.
* Proven track record leading critical, high-visibility projects or turnarounds across multiple manufacturing sites required.
* Working knowledge of FSMA, HACCP, Preventive Controls, GMPs, and GFSI-benchmarked standards (SQF, BRCGS, or similar) required
* Experience with sanitary design principles and capital project support preferred
* Experience with quality management systems and data analysis tools preferred

**Certifications:** PCQI and/or HACCP certification and Lean Six Sigma Green Belt or equivalent continuous improvement certification preferred
 
 
**Skills:** 

* Strong root cause analysis and data analysis skills, with the ability to quickly assess complex, ambiguous situations and determine what matters most.
* Ability to scope, prioritize, and execute multiple concurrent projects across sites, adjusting quickly as critical issues emerge.
* Builds trust and credibility quickly with plant teams, executives, customers, and regulators to drive results with teams that do not report to them.
* Strong written and verbal communication at all levels, and comfortable shifting between sites, projects, and priorities in a high-travel role.

Work Environment & Physical Demands
 

* 70% travel to manufacturing facilities
* Work in manufacturing environments that may include exposure to noise, varying temperatures, allergens, and moving equipment.
* Ability to stand and walk for extended periods, climb stairs and ladders, and carry light loads.
* Must comply with all GMP, food safety, and safety requirements, including use of required personal protective equipment.

The information provided in this document provides an overview of the most common duties, qualifications, and demands of the position. It is not intended to be a comprehensive summary of the role, and the duties, qualifications, and demands of the position are subject to change without notice. The expectations provided here may also be modified if an employee with a disability could effectively meet the expectations for the role with reasonable accommodation.
 
The pay range for this full-time, salaried position is $141,436-$212,154/year. Individual base pay depends on work location and additional factors such as experience, job-related skills, and relevant education or training. The position is eligible for a discretionary annual incentive based on company and individual performance. We offer a comprehensive benefits package including health, dental, 401k and wellness benefits beginning on the first day of employment.
 
 
Maker's Pride is an Equal Opportunity Employer.

**Job Title:** Global Director, Supplier Quality

**Job Location:** Southfield, MI

**What we offer:**

VeoneerSafety Systemsis the world leader in Automotive Electronic Safety Systems. Veoneer’s scalable, best-in-class restraint control systems are mitigating the effects of a car crash. To date, we have delivered more than 1 billion devices to car manufacturers globally.
 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems has an international and collaborative team of 2,700 employees in 11 countries. We empower our people and are dedicated to their professional development and growth*.* 
 
Veoneer Safety Systems – Protect Everyone in Every Crash.

**What you'll do:**

The Global Director of Supplier Quality leads the global SQ organization, setting strategy, standards, and accountability for supplier readiness, performance, and continuous improvement.

The role combines global Supplier Quality leadership (80%) with North America Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leadership (20%).

**Key Responsibilities for Supplier Quality** (80% of role)

**Strategic Leadership & Global Deployment**

* Set global SQ strategy aligned with corporate, customer, sourcing, and manufacturing objectives.
* Define and execution of Supplier Quality Policies, Standards, Processes, Methods and Systems.
* Owner of Veoneer Supplier Manual (VSM), Supplier Quality Project (SQP) – APQP & PPAP, Supplier Non-Conformance Material (NCM) Management.
* Align cross-functional priorities, resources, and accountability; establish SQE oversight of workload, open issues, owners, overdue actions, and escalations.
* Monitor supplier quality targets, initiatives and indicators to ensure compliance to Veoneer Supplier Quality related policies, standards and reporting.

**Supplier Development & Standards Compliance**

* Oversee new supplier assessment, qualification, and development with Purchasing and Engineering; improve assessment models and ensure teams close risks and capability gaps before sourcing and production approval.
* Set common supplier requirements, risk-based audit and development expectations, and change controls; ensure existing suppliers improve capability and sustain company and customer compliance.
* Representing quality in Supplier Sourcing Board.

**Supplier Performance & Major Quality Issues**

* Lead major supplier escalations with supplier executives and cross-functional teams, ensuring containment, exposure assessment, production and customer protection, and verified permanent corrective actions.
* Drive common KPIs and improvement targets for supplier PPM, repeat defects, corrective-action aging, disruptions.
* Require leadership reviews and improvement plans for systemic issues, sharing lessons learned across suppliers.
* Supplier Scorecard (VS051 rating) and drive continuous improvement for supplier quality performance.

**Supplier APQP / PPAP & Safe Launch**

* Ensure on time and effective supplier APQP, PPAP, and Safe Launch for new programs, suppliers, and changes, including risk reviews, capability verification, and readiness-gap closure before production release.

**Quality Tools, Talent Development & Training**

* Set expectations for consistent SQE application of core quality tools, process audits, and structured problem solving to strengthen prevention and corrective-action effectiveness.
* Assess global SQ team capabilities and set development priorities with regional managers to strengthen technical expertise, expand skills, and build future leaders through training, mentoring, and succession planning.
* Supplier Quality talent review and succession plan.

**Regional Leadership: Engineering Quality & Operational Quality** (20% of role)

* Represent Quality Leadership team in regional activities across RDE, Manufacturing and Supplier Quality teams.
* Align regional priorities, governance, performance reviews, and escalations with global Engineering Quality and Operational Quality leaders and standards.
* Guide development and launch readiness, quality system execution, major issue resolution, and lessons learned while retaining local execution accountability.

**What you'll bring:**

**Education:** Bachelor’s degree in engineering.

**Experience:** Minimum 15 years in supplier quality, including supplier qualification, development, major issue resolution, and talent development. Electronics experience required; automotive SQ experience strongly preferred. Experience leading a multinational organization is preferred.

**Skills:**

* Global SQ leadership and effective matrix-team management.
* Cross-functional influence, supplier executive engagement, and timely decision-making.
* Strong supplier APQP, PPAP, change management, and Safe Launch knowledge.
* Advanced PFMEA, control plan, MSA, SPC, capability, audit, and 8D expertise; proven data-driven problem resolution and daily management.
* Strong commodity expertise for IC, PCB and/or mechanical parts is preferred.
* Ability to work effectively across cultures and time zones.
* Experience in other Quality domains is preferred

**Location:** Physical location Markham, Ontario, Canada or Southfield, Michigan; global scope across North America, Europe, India, and Asia.

**Travel:** International travel will be required 8-10 times per year.

**Reporting / Collaboration:**

* Reports to SVP Manufacturing & Quality.
* Solid-line responsibility for tech-center SQEs; dotted-line functional leadership of plant SQEs, with plant leadership retaining local operational accountability.
* Partners with Purchasing, Operations, Engineering, Industrialization, Program Management, and supplier leadership.

* In coordination with the Clinical Performance team, train on data definitions, data interpretation and data analysis

* Adhere to CCNC privacy and security policies to ensure that patient and company data are properly safeguarded.

* Provide oversight and guidance to staff through a team approach that allows for coordinated handoffs, communication, and workflow across provider-facing staff
* Develop strategies for allocating QI resources to meet program goals and to control costs through effective use of personnel.

* Complete performance evaluations.
* Utilize conflict resolution and problem-solving skills to manage issues in a timely manner.

* Registered Nurse (BSN required; MSN preferred); Social Worker (BSW required; MSW and LCSW preferred); or master's in public health or health care administration. If RN: Active, unrestricted RN license to practice in North Carolina.
* At least 5 years of Quality Improvement or relevant health care experience with responsibilities in the following areas: operational leadership, process improvement, project management, systems analysis, data analytics, and team facilitation.
* At least 3 years of supervisory or leadership experience in health care.
* NAHQ Certified Professional in Healthcare Quality (CPHQ)
* Lean / Six Sigma certification a plus.
* Maintain a valid NC driver’s license with current auto liability insurance.

Excellent communication skills

* - oral, written and public speaking
* Knowledge of government, private sector and community resources
* Knowledge of and compliance with federal and state regulations applicable to the position
* Critical thinking skills, effective clinical judgment, independent decision making, and problem- solving abilities
* Skilled in establishing rapport with providers, community partners, and members
* Strong organizational and time management skills
* Demonstrated leadership skills
* Ability to work independently and function as an integral part of the team
* Expertise with Microsoft Office suite of products and comfort with database software and the internet
* Strong competence in quality improvement methodologies, principles, and recognition programs
* Ability to take “deep dives” into multiple sources of data to drive improvement
* Ability to stimulate innovative thinking & serve as a change agent
* Able to shift strategy or approach in response to the demands of a situation

* Potential for minor physical inconveniences or discomforts in the work setting, including sitting for moderate periods of time.
* Repetitive wrist motion and occasional lifting/carrying of up to 25 pounds.
* Travel required within the region and/or the state.
